name: 1Password
whyPeoplePay: 1Password sells the part a password manager lives or dies on: sync that has never lost anyone's vault, apps on every platform a family actually owns, and recovery when someone forgets the one password that matters. You are paying for an operator who is awake at 3am, not for the cryptography.

plans.name: Individual
plans.note: Billed monthly. $2.99/mo if paid annually, advertised as a first-year rate for new customers.

plans.name: Families
plans.note: Billed monthly, covers up to 5 people. $4.49/mo if paid annually, advertised as a first-year rate for new customers.

plans.name: Teams Starter Pack
plans.note: Flat rate for the first 10 members, paid annually.

plans.name: Business
plans.note: Per user per month, paid annually.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Quote only — the page says request a quote.

pricing.note: Personal and Families read from 1password.com/personal; Teams Starter Pack and Business from 1password.com/business-pricing on the same day. We record the monthly-billed figure for Individual and Families because the annual figure is an introductory first-year rate, and savings math built on an introductory rate overstates the saving in year two.

ranked.rationale: The only one on this list that speaks the Bitwarden protocol, so the official Bitwarden apps and browser extensions on every platform your household already uses point at your server without knowing the difference. That client story is the whole reason a self-hosted vault is usable by people who did not choose to self-host.
